chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
When you pray behind an Imam whom you follow, then do not recite behind him, whether you hear his recitation or do not hear it.

So this does not contradict what we have presented before: that whenever he does not hear the recitation in a prayer in which the recitation is said aloud, then he should recite. That is because it is possible that the narrator transmitted only part of the hadith, for we have already presented in the narration of ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, this very hadith, and he added: “unless it is a prayer in which recitation is aloud and you do not hear, then recite.”

And if this is part of the complete report, then it agrees with the rest of the reports. It is also possible that what is meant by that is when he hears the recitation, but hears it faintly such that it is not distinguishable to him, like a murmur; then that also suffices for him. And that which indicates this is:

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader being followed in congregational salat
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: other narrations on the same issue
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ: the report or narration in full form
key_terms.تَأْتَمُّ: you follow in prayer behind an Imam

ai.seo_question: Should a person recite behind the Imam in congregational salat if the Imam’s recitation is not heard?
ai.summary: This report concerns the ruling on recitation when praying behind an Imam whom one follows in congregational prayer. It presents a reconciliation between narrations by explaining that non-recitation applies generally, while recitation is allowed in aloud prayers when the follower does not hear the Imam’s recitation.
